slides.heading: Symmetrical Tree
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Symmetrical Tree, a medium binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Is the tree a mirror image of itself around its root?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Is the tree a mirror image of itself around its root?

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A tree is symmetric if the left subtree mirrors the right.
slides.narration: A tree is symmetric if the left subtree mirrors the right.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Build the mirror tree and compare → O(n) time, O(n) space
Recursive pairwise mirror check → O(n), O(h) space
Or BFS checking each level is a palindrome
slides.narration: You could build a mirrored copy and compare, using extra memory. Better is checking pairs directly: the left subtree's outer child pairs with the right subtree's outer child, and inner with inner.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Compare two nodes at a time
3. Outer children pair together and inner children pair together
slides.narration: Step by step. First, compare two nodes at a time. Second, values must match. Third, outer children pair together and inner children pair together.

slides.narration: Compare the mirrored pair: 2 on the left with 2 on the right. They match, so continue with outer and inner children.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Mirror returns true if both nodes are null and false if just one is. Otherwise values must be equal, and we recursively compare left's left with right's right, and left's right with right's left.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: One side null, the other not → false
Values must match, not just shapes
slides.narration: If one side is null and the other isn't, return false. Both structure and values must mirror.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Iterative with a queue of pairs
slides.narration: An iterative version uses a queue of node pairs. Note that a tree is symmetric when it equals its own inversion.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A tree is symmetric if the left subtree mirrors the right.
slides.narration: To recap Symmetrical Tree: A tree is symmetric if the left subtree mirrors the right. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
